title: No source gives the wire shape or the value sets this story needs: the append request and answer, the ledger read and its page, the reference-data operation, the text of MSG-P7-009 and the DP-02 login name
source: Legacy RWB-E2-032 sections 7, 8, 10, 12, 13 and 14 against TSD P7 v2 T3.1, T3.2, T-A.1 and T-A.2, FSD P7 v3 A2.2.4.3 and A2.5, and Architecture v5 slide 20
description: The legacy story fixes the facts of the decision record and none of the shapes. It gives the decision code D5 and the final call SUGGESTION_RECORDED as literals of its decision log mapping, and neither TSD P7 v2 T3.2 nor any LOV table the extract carries lists the values of LOV-DECISION or a final-call list, so both are carried as reference data whose values are read and not written. It gives the mapping field by field but no request or answer body: the append has no path and no method in the service, because TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 documents only the two reads API-P7-006 and API-P7-007, and the field set of the DecisionLogPage and of the DecisionLogEntry the reads return is not written out. The run read of rwb-agent is consumed without a documented request or answer, and the reference-data operation the decision code and the final call are read through is not named by any source. The text of MSG-P7-009 is named by FSD P7 v3 A2.2.4.3 and written out nowhere. The name of the per-service database login of DP-02 is not given. The only shapes the legacy gives are the decision log mapping, the inputs reference as a masked inputs snapshot, the actions {treatmentId, agentRunId} and the key TDR_OFFER:<treatmentId>.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-032 section 8 BR3 ('A suggestion is returned only after its decision log entry is written'), BR5 and BR6; section 10 (roles RW-RESTRUCT, RW-CASEOWN, SY-AGENT, SY-DECLOG, RW-COE, RW-RISK); section 12 (decision log mapping with case_id, decision_code D5, model_version, agent_version null, inputs_ref, recommendation, final_call SUGGESTION_RECORDED, actions, and the idempotency key); section 13 (TDR_OFFER policy P1 and P2); section 14 (MSG-P10-007, MSG-P7-003, MSG-P4-002); TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (decision_log_entry DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-031), T3.2 (LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL, LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-PRODUCT and no LOV-DECISION) and T-A.1 (API-P7-006, API-P7-007); FSD P7 v3 A2.2.4.3 AC-EXC-P7-002-05 (MSG-P7-009 naming decisionCode) and A2.5 (a failed decision log write blocks the action); Architecture v5 slide 20 (every service writes its own decision records) and slide 41 (schema and login per service)
proposed: Agree the three operation shapes, the two list value sets and the message text at the wave 2 contract review of RWB-P10-E2032-CON and of this service: the append on POST /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log with the request and the DecisionRecord answer of section 12.1, the two reads with the DecisionLogPage and DecisionLogEntry field sets of TSD P7 v2 T3.1, LOV-DECISION with the value D5, a final-call list with SUGGESTION_RECORDED, the reference-data operation path, the text of MSG-P7-009 and the name of the rwb-decision login. Until then the story builds and tests against the values of ASM-B2-P7-003-1 to ASM-B2-P7-003-3 and the contract fakes of section 12.8.

title: The metadata rows name no build dependency and the agent contract only, while the DP table of the story adds five platform contracts and two rwb-case contracts and the story consumes a further authorise operation
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP table rows DP-01, DP-03, DP-05, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-11, DP-13 and DP-19 against the plan story record of RWB-P7-E2032-APP, the Ownership Map and Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41
description: The story record carries Depends on (build) None and Contract dependencies RWB-P10-E2032-CON. The nine patterns the story applies add seven contracts the metadata does not carry: DP-03 H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, DP-06 H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and C RWB-P3-E1042-CON, DP-07 H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON, DP-09 H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON and DP-19 H RWB-PLT-N001-CON. DP-01, DP-05, DP-11 and DP-13 add none. One operation the story consumes is named by no pattern and by no metadata row: the P4 authorise call of the Decision log right, because DP-08 is not among the patterns of the key. The legacy key also depends on RWB-E1-058 (the model gateway client), RWB-E2-004 (the treatment record) and RWB-E1-027 (the decision log writer), which in the target are carried by RWB-P10-E2032-CON, by `rwb-treatment` (S2) and by RWB-PLT-E1027-CON respectively and not by a row of this story. Each dependency is a platform contract of waves 0 and 1 or a published contract of another service, so none blocks the build beyond Day 1, but a worker cannot choose between the plan line and the pattern table without a ruling.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 rows DP-01, DP-03, DP-05, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-11, DP-13 and DP-19 and R5.7 rules 1 to 3; the story record of RWB-P7-E2032-APP (H [], C ['RWB-P10-E2032-CON']); legacy RWB-E2-032 section 3 (RWB-E1-058, RWB-E2-004, RWB-E1-027) and section 10 (the Decision log right R); Ownership Map api row GET /cases/{caseId} (P3) and table decision_log_entry (P7); Architecture v5 slide 14 (P4 IN: POST /authorise) and slide 41 (P4 first API path /authorise); sections 3, 12.2 and 13 of this story
proposed: Read the H list of the story as None plus the five platform contracts the DP table names, and the C list as RWB-P10-E2032-CON plus C RWB-P3-E1042-CON, C RWB-P3-E1043-CON and the published contract of the P4 authorise call; the platform contracts are delivery prerequisites of the service template and not per-story blockers, and the story stays Day 1.
